name: TPS2065CDBVR
title: Current-limited single power-distribution switches, 0.5 A to 2 A
summary: The TPS20xxC and TPS20xxC-2 are single high-side power switches for 5 V rails such as USB ports, built around an N-channel MOSFET with its own charge pump. Each part number has a fixed, flat constant-current limit (0.5 A, 1 A, 1.5 A or 2 A rated parts, ±20 %), an enable input of either polarity, an open-drain fault flag with a 9 ms deglitch, undervoltage lockout, thermal shutdown and reverse blocking while off. TPS20xxC parts pull the output down through about 470 Ω when off; TPS20xxC-2 parts have no discharge. TPS2065CDBVR is the 1 A, active-high enable, with-discharge part in the 5-pin SOT-23.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A TPS20xxC or TPS20xxC-2 passes the supply on IN to the load on OUT. IN has a 0.1 µF capacitor to ground, OUT a polarised 150 µF to ground. The open-drain fault flag is pulled up to the input rail by 10 kΩ and leaves as the fault signal; a control signal drives the enable pin, whose polarity is set by the part number. GND and, on the DGN package only, the PowerPAD go to ground.

parts.note: any part of the family; PAD exists on DGN only

circuits.title: Typical application, TPS2065CDGN
circuits.description: A TPS2065CDGN switches a 4.5 V to 6.5 V input onto VOUT. The input has 0.1 µF to ground; the output capacitor COUT goes to ground. RFAULT pulls the fault pin up to the input and the same node is the fault signal output. A control signal drives EN (active high on this part). GND (pin 1) and the PowerPAD both go to ground.

equations.name: Dissipation in current limit
equations.note: This dissipation is what drives the junction into thermal cycling during a long overload.

operation.text: Ten part numbers cover rated currents 0.5 A, 1 A, 1.5 A and 2 A; enable active high or active low; output discharge on TPS20xxC parts and absent on TPS20xxC-2 parts. The device comparison table gives each combination and package. The parts are pin compatible with earlier TI switches.

The switch stays off until IN rises past the UVLO threshold (3.75 V typ). About 0.14 V of hysteresis keeps a supply dip caused by a large current surge from toggling it. FLT is high impedance while in UVLO.

EN (or EN with bar) switches the power FET and also the bias of the charge pump, driver and other blocks, so a disabled part draws under 1 µA. Disabling clears an active fault flag. The input accepts TTL and CMOS levels. It must be driven or tied to VIN or GND as the part requires; it must not float.

tON and tOFF are an internal delay plus the output rise or fall time. Rise time is set by the part together with the load, mostly its capacitance. On TPS20xxC parts the fall time depends on the load R and C and the internal pulldown RPD; TPS20xxC-2 parts have no RPD, so only the load sets it. With a purely resistive load the part's own tF applies; with R and C in parallel the R × C time constant wins when it is longer than tF.

operation.topic: Charge pump, soft start and reverse blocking
operation.text: An internal charge pump lifts the gate of the N-channel FET above its source. The driver shapes the output ramp in both directions, giving a built-in soft start and limiting surges on the input supply. When the switch is off, whether by UVLO or by enable, the FET blocks current flowing back from OUT to IN.

In overload the part holds the output current at the static IOS value and the output voltage settles at IOS × RLOAD. Two cases: (1) powering up or enabling into an existing short: the output stays near 0 V and the current ramps to IOS; (2) an overload arriving while fully on: the part reacts within tIOS, either settling straight to IOS or briefly turning off and returning in a controlled way to IOS, depending on overload size, input circuit and how fast it is applied. In both cases the limit holds until the overload goes away or thermal cycling begins.

A long overload heats the die through (VIN – VOUT) × IOS. In current limit the part turns off once TJ passes 135 °C (min), stays off until it has cooled by 20 °C, then restarts, repeating while the fault lasts. Out of current limit the shutdown threshold is 155 °C (min).

Many older switches overshoot to a higher corner current IOC before falling back to IOS (a peaking characteristic). These parts show no noticeable peaking: the I-V curve goes flat at IOS, so no IOC is specified.

FLT is an open-drain, active-low output that goes low on overcurrent or overtemperature. A 9 ms deglitch filters both the falling and rising edges, so start-up and short transients are not reported. An overcurrent shorter than the deglitch period resets the timer when it ends; separate short overloads do not add up to a fault, and the same holds when leaving a fault. Heavy input ripple with a large output capacitance can push the part in and out of current limit near IOS and disturb the flag. If the overtemperature circuit trips while in current limit, FLT goes low at once, but its release is still deglitched. The flag trips as the knee of constant-current limiting is reached. Disabling releases FLT the moment the switch opens, and FLT is high impedance whenever the part is disabled or in UVLO.

TPS20xxC parts connect a 470 Ω (typ) pulldown from OUT to ground when in UVLO or disabled, draining stored charge and leakage. The pulldown loses bias as VIN falls, so its resistance rises as VIN approaches 0 V. TPS20xxC-2 parts lack it; their output in those states is set by the external load alone. There are no other operating modes.

A TPS2065CDGN on a 5 V ±0.5 V rail feeding a USB 3.0 port: the port may draw 900 mA, so the minimum current limit has to sit above 900 mA to avoid false trips, which the 1 A TPS2065C meets. The maximum current limit, 1.8 A for the TPS2065C, has to sit below what the upstream supply can deliver so the switch protects it. The inputs to the design are the normal input voltage, the continuous output current and the upstream supply's maximum current.

Always fit a ceramic bypass of 0.1 µF or more from IN to GND as close as possible. Input overshoot has two causes: a supply applied abruptly through bus inductance into the input capacitance while IN is still high impedance (ideally up to twice the applied voltage), and input inductance driving IN high when the part cuts off a short-circuit current. Large load steps and output shorts can also make the input droop. With long supply leads a large input capacitance may be needed to keep the peak under the absolute maximum. A ceramic of 1 µF to 22 µF next to IN both speeds the response and limits the transient on the input bus. Brief input transients to 6.5 V are allowed.

Right after a short, output-side inductance (for example a cable) keeps current flowing as the switch cuts back, pulling OUT down and possibly below ground; a large output capacitor limits this. USB applications need at least 120 µF on the output, usually a 150 µF electrolytic. Where 120 µF is not needed but OUT could still be driven negative, use at least 10 µF of ceramic. Keep the undershoot under 1.5 V for 10 µs.
Run the parts from a 4.5 V to 5.5 V supply able to deliver more than the switch's maximum current limit.

Put the 100 nF bypass by IN and GND and the at-least-10 µF low-ESR ceramic by OUT and GND, each with a low-inductance connection. Connect the PowerPAD straight to the ground plane with wide, short copper.

DBV example: GND copper 0.052 in² total with 3 vias of 0.018 in; VIN copper 0.00925 in² with 3 vias of 0.018 in; VOUT copper 0.041 in² total with 4 vias of 0.01 in and a 0.050 in trace. DGN example: GND 0.056 in² total with 3 vias of 0.018 in; VIN 0.0145 in² with 2 vias of 0.018 in; VOUT 0.048 in² total with 5 vias of 0.01 in and a 0.050 in trace. DGK example: copper areas of 0.100 × 0.175 in with 5 vias of 18 mil, 0.185 × 0.045 in with 3 vias of 18 mil, 0.100 × 0.060 in with 3 vias of 18 mil to inner plane 2, 0.08 × 0.250 in, 0.15 × 0.15 in and 0.07 × 0.08 in, with 50 mil and 10 mil traces.

Extra copper around the part lowers its thermal impedance; soldering the DGN pad lowers TJ further. The RθJACustom values come from the layout examples on a JEDEC high-k board (two signal and two plane layers, four layers of 1 oz copper); they do not include nearby heat sources or changed airflow. Where the DGN pad cannot be soldered (to route under the chip, for example) its θJA without extra copper is about 141 °C/W for 0.5 A and 1 A parts and 139 °C/W for 1.5 A and 2 A parts; the DGK package, which has no pad, measures 110.3 °C/W on its example layout.
The family is UL listed under CB file E169910.
